content.text: Xiaomeng, look at this! I just came across a co-branded cat food advertisement between a pet brand and an illustrator. The pattern of the Shiba Inu sticking out its tongue is trending, and the art style is super cute! It reminds me of that adorable head-tilt shot of our "Boss" catching a frisbee in the park. If it were made into merchandise, it would definitely be popular too.

Wow, this design is really cozy. The purple color scheme paired with the cat illustrations feels perfect for the pet community style we planned earlier. Where did you see it? This warm vibe reminds me of that aesthetic game skin you shared before, the one with the green long hair and floral elements.

On a design platform, they also released merchandise like phone cases and tote bags. Look at this picture—the cartoon dog pattern is printed on various daily items, which is quite creative. This reminds me of our discussion when we set up social media accounts for 'Boss.' Combining online and offline efforts enhances interaction, and merchandise is a great offline extension, isn't it?

Hmm, such co-branded products really do attract fans, just like the inspiration for our exploration videos we discussed after our last gathering—both turn interesting experiences into content. But, Xingchen, do you think we could also do something similar? For example, having 'the boss' collaborate with my ragdoll cat to create merchandise? Like the theme from our first offline pet meetup poster, 'Social Butterfly Shiba Inu vs. Aloof Ragdoll'—the contrast in cuteness would definitely have market appeal.

Haha, I knew you'd be interested! I was just about to bring it up. Our super-social Shiba Inu and aloof Ragdoll cat—what a contrast in cuteness! They’d definitely be a hit. You organized that pet mixer so successfully before, covering everything from the event flow to risk management. This time, we could try co-branded product development. Just like how we went from losing streaks in games to teaming up to rank up, and then planning a beginner-friendly murder mystery party—we’re exploring new areas step by step!

Sounds good, but we need to seriously consider the feasibility. First, where do we find suppliers? We can’t produce them ourselves, so we need to find reliable ones, just like we did for the group purchase of pet supplies. Remember the thank-you banquet we held after the first successful group purchase in our pet community? We discussed back then about acting within our means and controlling the budget.

Don't worry, I have some ideas here. Look at this picture—there are pet aprons, logo designs, and it seems like there's a high demand for pet collar products. We could look for OEM factories or partner with brands, just like negotiating collaborations with escape room shops. I recently took on a new client for advertising planning and have been building up business resources, so we could give it a try.

That makes sense, but how do we control the costs? We need to calculate everything clearly and avoid going over budget like we did with the last appreciation banquet. Also, what about the design? We can't just sketch it out randomly—we need a professional illustrator. Remember what we discussed about game skin collections? Skins aren't just about appearance; they can also enhance the experience, so the quality of the design is crucial.

I'll handle the design—my role as a creative planner at the ad agency isn't for nothing; I'm quick on my feet! But we really do need to find a good illustrator. Any recommendations? Just like how you were so meticulous when finding a DM—someone patient enough to guide a group of newbies through a script-killing game.

Well, I suggest you check out some design websites, like this platform that focuses on creative design and advertising, where there are many illustrators' works. We can look for inspiration here or directly contact the bloggers. This reminds me of when you shared the game hero rankings with me for reference—practical information always helps a lot.

Great idea! You're always so thoughtful and well-organized. I'll go ahead and browse around to find an illustrator who fits our pet's style, just as reliable as the hero rankings you recommended in the game before. By the way, do you remember my dramatic flair during my livestreams? This design might also need a touch of humor to reflect the "boss's" social butterfly personality.

Yes, and there's this design resource website. Take the Year of the Horse theme as an example, but it offers a variety of styles. You can search for pet-related materials. Look, here it says, 'Professional designers find inspiration on Huaban.' We can draw inspiration from that. Just like when we were planning the pet fan community, we referenced the structure of your game hero rankings—clarity of information is crucial.

Awesome! Xiaomeng, you're truly my golden partner, always offering practical advice from gaming losing streaks to pet activities. So, let's decide to try developing the 'Social Butterfly Shiba Inu & Aloof Ragdoll' co-branded merchandise and set up a micro-project, shall we? Just like how we went from sharing game skins to managing pet accounts, step by step turning fun ideas into reality.

I agree! It's just like when we planned the beginner session for the script murder game before, which required precise division of labor. I can take charge of researching suppliers and cost control, while you handle creative design and liaising with illustrators, reflecting our mutual growth. Remember how efficient we were when we divided tasks to plan the pet social event? I'm sure we'll collaborate just as smoothly this time.

Perfect! Fun is the top priority, connecting people. This collaboration product is sure to make our pet community more active. I’ll start by finding a few illustrator samples, and then we can discuss the details step by step, just like sharing game skins. Who knows, maybe we can even design exclusive merchandise for our core fans, just like we exchange skins, to strengthen our bond.

Alright, Star. Remember to keep your sense of humor and don't be too dramatic, okay? I'll conduct market research simultaneously to ensure the project's feasibility. Just like how we ensured harmony in pet activities before, this time we also need to balance fun and practicality. So, let's wrap up this conversation for now. Shall we schedule our next discussion to review the progress?

No problem! See you next time. I look forward to our pet collaboration ideas sprouting and blossoming, just as smoothly as the video project that followed the Clean Plate Campaign! From gaming to pets, and now product development, our exploration team is becoming more and more impressive—no room for boredom!
